intent: Show a page-level status message that sits in the flow of the page rather than interrupting it.
typical_uses: A status message tied to the current page or section
Pairing a short instruction with an optional action the user can take without leaving the page

dont_use_when.situation: A message the user must acknowledge or dismiss before continuing

instead.target: toast() rendered by a mounted Toaster

dont_use_when.situation: A validation message tied to one form control

invariants.text: The root renders role="alert" by default, so assistive tech announces it as soon as it mounts.

Any direct <svg> child switches Alert to the two-column icon layout, and every direct <svg> child is placed as an icon: sized to the small icon box and spanning both rows. An <svg> nested deeper, inside a part, is not detected.
When an AlertAction is present as a direct child, the alert reserves a fixed amount of additional padding on its own right edge so body text never runs under it.

anti_patterns.dont: Put more than one direct <svg> child in an Alert
anti_patterns.do_instead: Use one leading <svg>; every direct <svg> is laid out as an icon, so a second one takes a grid cell meant for the title or description

a11y.by: alert.test.tsx asserts screen.getByRole('alert') resolves the rendered root, confirming role="alert" is present by default

good.title: An icon-led alert with a destructive variant and a corner action
good.code:
<Alert variant="destructive">
  <WarningIcon />
  <AlertTitle>Payment failed</AlertTitle>
  <AlertDescription>We couldn't charge your card ending in 4242.</AlertDescription>
  <AlertAction>
    <Button size="sm" variant="outline">Retry</Button>
  </AlertAction>
</Alert>

bad.title: Two leading icons on one alert
bad.why: Every direct <svg> child is sized and placed as an icon spanning both rows, so the second icon lands in the column the title and description need and pushes them out of line.
